facts.label: Strongest contrary evidence and limitations
facts.text: 1. Covenants. The covenant package is named but not quantified: "requires the maintenance of a maximum Secured Net Leverage Ratio and a minimum Consolidated Interest Coverage Ratio (as defined in the Credit Agreement), in each case, with the levels set forth in the Credit Agreement" (10-Q_2026-09-30_alks-20260930.htm.jsonl page:28), and compliance is a management statement only: "The Company was in compliance with its debt covenants at September 30, 2026." (page:30). The text carves out the Term Loan B from the maintenance tests. Mechanism: without levels, defined terms and add-back rules, headroom cannot be computed from the statements, so any leverage or coverage view is a computed ratio, not the covenant measure. 2. Period comparability. The business combination closed on February 12, 2026, so nine months 2026 contains Avadel results only from that date, while FY2025 and nine months 2025 contain none. The company states that "the presentation of net (loss) income is impracticable due to the integration of Avadel’s operations" (10-Q_2026-09-30_alks-20260930.htm.jsonl page:19). Unaudited pro forma revenue and net income are given in the same note, as a separate comparative basis. Consequence: trend statements across FY2025 and 2026 need the pro forma note and explicit labelling. 3. Preliminary accounting. "The Company’s purchase price allocation is preliminary" (10-Q_2026-09-30_alks-20260930.htm.jsonl page:16, in the note text "purchase price allocation is preliminary and based on the information available as of the reporting date"); goodwill and intangibles can still move for up to one year from closing. 4. Liquidity structure. No revolving facility, undrawn commitment or letter of credit facility is described in any pinned source (searches for "revolv" returned no match in all seven sources). The only letters of credit mentioned are collateralised by held-to-maturity investments tied to leases (10-Q_2026-09-30_alks-20260930.htm.jsonl page:50). Liquidity therefore equals cash and investments in the sources, and the absence of a revolver is a finding of the searched text, not proof the issuer has none. 5. Management add-backs. The nine-month reconciliation adds back share-based compensation of 112,624 thousand (EX-99.1_2026-11-03_alks-ex99_1.htm.jsonl page:6) while the cash flow statement shows 94,216 thousand (10-Q_2026-09-30_alks-20260930.htm.jsonl page:7). The difference is unexplained in the pack and is carried as a conflict below.

facts.label: Financial base view
facts.text: The financial base is adequate for a credit snapshot of the post-acquisition Alkermes, with the limits stated here. Before February 12, 2026 the company was unlevered: no debt at December 31, 2025, 388.6 US$m of cash and equivalents, 199.8 US$m of investments and 731.2 US$m of restricted cash held in escrow for the Avadel acquisition. The acquisition cost 2,199.2 US$m in cash plus a contingent value right, funded by 1,525.0 US$m of term loans (net proceeds 1,511.6 US$m) and balance sheet cash. At September 30, 2026 the balance sheet carries 1,497.7 US$m of term loan debt (net of 14.0 US$m of discount and fees), 787.6 US$m of cash and investments and no restricted cash. LTM revenue is 1,753.6 US$m against 1,475.9 US$m in FY2025, mostly from the addition of LUMRYZ. GAAP profit is near zero over the LTM because of inventory step-up amortization, acquisition costs, intangible amortization, a contingent consideration fair value charge and 86.6 US$m of interest expense, and the management measures are the main bridge to leverage. On the management Adjusted EBITDA basis, total debt is 3.40 times LTM and net debt 1.61 times; on the company-definition reported EBITDA the same ratios are 10.25 and 4.86 times. The covenant package, the margin grid and any revolver are not readable from the pack, so headroom, undrawn liquidity and cash coverage are Not supplied. Debt service is modest through 2030 (scheduled amortization of 6.6 to 45.3 US$m a year) with nearly all principal due in 2031, which places the refinancing test in 2031.

facts.text: EBITDA definitions. Reported EBITDA is the company measure: "EBITDA represents earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortization." (EX-99.1_2026-11-03_alks-ex99_1.htm.jsonl page:3), reconciled from net income by deducting interest income and adding interest expense, tax, depreciation and amortization of acquired intangibles (page:6). Adjusted EBITDA is management's measure: "Adjusted EBITDA excludes share-based compensation expense and non-recurring gains or losses in addition to the components of EBITDA from earnings." (page:3). For nine months 2026 the add-backs are share-based compensation of 112.6 US$m, costs related to the acquisition of Avadel of 118.1 US$m and the contingent consideration fair value change of 27.0 US$m (page:6). Neither measure is a covenant measure; the credit agreement defines Secured Net Leverage Ratio and Consolidated Interest Coverage Ratio, and those definitions are Not supplied. Total debt in this handoff is the balance sheet carrying amount of the term loans (current portion plus long-term debt); net debt deducts cash and equivalents plus short-term and long-term investments, which are not restricted. Operating leases, the contingent consideration and the litigation matters are outside the debt figure.

facts.label: Reported results
facts.text: Q3 2026 total revenues were 480.1 US$m against 394.2 US$m in Q3 2025, with product sales net of 417.3 US$m against 317.4 US$m (10-Q_2026-09-30_alks-20260930.htm.jsonl page:6). The 10-Q attributes the increase "primarily due to the addition of LUMRYZ to our proprietary product portfolio" (page:37). The release shows LUMRYZ net sales of 89.9 US$m for Q3 2026 and 226.0 US$m for nine months 2026, with no comparative because the product was acquired (EX-99.1_2026-11-03_alks-ex99_1.htm.jsonl page:1). Manufacturing and royalty revenues fell to 62.9 US$m in Q3 2026 from 76.8 US$m in Q3 2025 (10-Q_2026-09-30_alks-20260930.htm.jsonl page:6), and LYBALVI net sales slipped to 95.9 US$m from 98.2 US$m (EX-99.1_2026-11-03_alks-ex99_1.htm.jsonl page:1). Q3 2026 operating income was 36.0 US$m against 89.1 US$m, and GAAP net income was 16.3 US$m against 82.8 US$m, with interest expense of 27.6 US$m against nil (page:6-7). Nine months 2026 shows an operating income of 6.1 US$m and a net loss of 49.7 US$m. Quarterly Adjusted EBITDA was 80.3 US$m in Q1 2026, 139.2 US$m in Q2 2026 and 120.1 US$m in Q3 2026 (derived from the cumulative reconciliations; see Calculations), against 121.5 US$m in Q3 2025. Management reiterated its 2026 expectations in November (EX-99.1_2026-11-03_alks-ex99_1.htm.jsonl page:2); the July release sets out projected 2026 Adjusted EBITDA of 390.0 US$m at the mid-point of ranges (EX-99.1_2026-07-28_alks-ex99_1.htm.jsonl page:8), which is management guidance, not evidence.

facts.label: Debt and capital structure
facts.text: At September 30, 2026 the debt consists of two senior secured term loans under the February 12, 2026 credit agreement, as amended by Amendment No. 1 on August 12, 2026: Term Loan A Facility due February 12, 2031 at a carrying amount of 735.0 US$m and Term Loan B Facility due August 12, 2031 at 762.7 US$m, total 1,497.7 US$m, of which 26.5 US$m is current (10-Q_2026-09-30_alks-20260930.htm.jsonl pages:6 and 27). Scheduled principal is 1,511.75 US$m, and the company states "At September 30, 2026, our borrowings consisted of $1.511 billion outstanding under the Facilities." (page:55). Unamortized discount and fees are "$3.6 million and $10.4 million, respectively" (page:30). The facilities were drawn in full at closing at 1,525.0 US$m: "the Company borrowed the full $1.525 billion available under the Facilities" (10-K_2025-12-31_alks-20251231.htm.jsonl page:193). Pricing after the amendment is Term SOFR plus 1.75% to 2.25% on Term Loan A, set by a Secured Net Leverage Ratio grid that is not supplied, and Term SOFR plus 2.25% on Term Loan B; the amendment cut the spread by 0.75% on Term Loan A and 0.50% on Term Loan B (page:28). The original margin was 2.75% on both (10-Q_2026-03-31_alks-20260331.htm.jsonl page:23). Three-month SOFR was 4.07% at September 30, 2026, and the company estimates that a 10% rise in the rate would raise interest from October 1 to December 31, 2026 by $1.6 million (10-Q_2026-09-30_alks-20260930.htm.jsonl page:55).

facts.text: The Facilities are "guaranteed by subsidiary guarantors and secured by a lien on substantially all of the assets of the borrowers and the subsidiary guarantors" (page:28). All debt therefore ranks as senior secured with no unsecured or subordinated tranche; no other debt instrument appears in the debt note. The amendment was accounted for lender by lender, with three exiting Term Loan B lenders treated as extinguished and one new lender as new issuance (page:29), with a 0.5 US$m write-off of deferred costs and 2.6 US$m of arranger fees in Q3 interest expense.

facts.label: Debt and capital structure
facts.text: Claims outside the debt figure. (1) Operating leases: lease liabilities of 7.6 US$m current and 65.8 US$m long-term at September 30, 2026 (page:6); all leases are operating leases (10-K_2025-12-31_alks-20251231.htm.jsonl page:192) and the 10-Q reports "Cash paid for lease liabilities was $2.9 million and $8.6 million during the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026" (10-Q_2026-09-30_alks-20260930.htm.jsonl page:27). (5) Pensions, factoring and supply chain finance: no pension, factoring or supply chain finance arrangement was found in the 10-K or the September 10-Q text (searches returned no match), so these are Not supplied rather than nil.

facts.label: Liquidity
facts.text: Liquidity at September 30, 2026 is cash and cash equivalents of 631.3 US$m plus short-term investments of 124.2 US$m and long-term investments of 32.1 US$m, total 787.6 US$m, which the release states as "$787.6 million" (EX-99.1_2026-11-03_alks-ex99_1.htm.jsonl page:2). No revolving facility, undrawn committed facility or letter of credit line is described in any pinned source, so undrawn committed facilities are Not supplied and available liquidity is cash and investments only; this is the finding of the searched text and not proof that none exists. The only letters of credit mentioned are collateralised by held-to-maturity investments tied to leases (10-Q_2026-09-30_alks-20260930.htm.jsonl page:50). Cash fell to 351.6 US$m at March 31, 2026 as the acquisition closed and the escrow was used, then rose to 511.5 US$m at June 30 and 631.3 US$m at September 30. Management states: "We expect that our existing cash, cash equivalents and investments will be sufficient to finance our anticipated working capital and other cash requirements" (page:50). Near-term debt service is the 26.5 US$m current portion and interest; no facility expires within twelve months.

facts.label: Cash flow quality
facts.text: Cash flow from operations was 72.9 US$m for nine months 2026 against 350.7 US$m for nine months 2025 (10-Q_2026-09-30_alks-20260930.htm.jsonl page:7). The 2026 figure is after a net loss of 49.7 US$m, add-backs of 94.2 US$m share-based compensation, 76.9 US$m depreciation and amortization, 72.4 US$m inventory step-up amortization and 27.0 US$m contingent consideration fair value, and a working capital outflow of 156.8 US$m (page:51), including a 116.4 US$m outflow in accounts payable and accrued expenses (page:7). Capital expenditure was low at 15.6 US$m. Cash taxes paid were 34.9 US$m against 3.1 US$m (page:8). Free cash flow, defined here as cash from operations less additions of property, plant and equipment, was 57.3 US$m for nine months 2026 and 227.4 US$m over the LTM, against 480.3 US$m in FY2025. Q3 2026 alone generated 93.5 US$m of operating cash flow (derived by subtraction), which suggests recovery after the heavy first half, but one quarter is not a trend. Share-based compensation is large relative to Adjusted EBITDA: the release adds back 112.6 US$m of it in nine months 2026 against Adjusted EBITDA of 339.5 US$m. It is a non-cash but recurring cost, and the sources do not say whether it is settled in cash.

facts.label: Leverage and coverage
facts.text: Leverage. On total debt of 1,497.7 US$m (carrying) and LTM Adjusted EBITDA of 440.2 US$m (derived, see below), total debt to EBITDA is 3.40 times; net debt of 710.2 US$m gives 1.61 times. On principal of 1,511.75 US$m the ratios are 3.43 and 1.65 times. On LTM reported EBITDA of 146.2 US$m the ratios are 10.25 and 4.86 times. The gap between the bases is explained by add-backs of acquisition-related costs, share-based compensation and the inventory step-up that flows through cost of goods sold; the step-up is non-cash and, as an analyst inference, should roll off as the acquired inventory is sold, whereas share-based compensation is a recurring cost. At December 31, 2025 there was no debt; net debt was negative 588.4 US$m (cash 388.6 plus investments 199.8), and 731.2 US$m of restricted cash is excluded from that figure.

facts.text: Coverage. facts.label: Calculations
facts.text: 1. FY2025 EBITDA (company definition, derived). Net income 241,664 less interest income 45,304 plus interest expense 12,277 plus income tax provision 49,786 plus depreciation and amortization 27,165 = 285,588 (10-K_2025-12-31_alks-20251231.htm.jsonl pages:166 and 168). The same method reproduces the printed nine-month 2025 EBITDA: 192,323 less 33,174 plus nil plus 38,750 plus 23,319 = 221,218 against 221,217 printed (rounding). 2. FY2025 Adjusted EBITDA (derived, approximate). EBITDA 285,588 plus share-based compensation 98,716 (10-K page:168) plus Avadel acquisition costs of "approximately $10.0 million" incurred in the fourth quarter of 2025 (10-K page:130, stated in millions) = 394,304. Nine-month 2025 Adjusted EBITDA of 293,658 equals EBITDA 221,217 plus share-based compensation 72,441 with no acquisition costs, so the only 2025 add-backs through September were share-based compensation. Implied Q4 2025 Adjusted EBITDA is 394,304 less 293,658 = 100,646. The approximation lies in the 10.0 US$m rounded cost and in whether the company would add back exactly that amount. 3. LTM Sep 30, 2026 EBITDA = 285,588 + 81,798 - 221,217 = 146,169. LTM Adjusted EBITDA = 394,304 + 339,544 - 293,658 = 440,190 (release page:6). Cross-check by quarters: 100,646 + 80,261 + 139,218 + 120,065 = 440,190, where Q1 is 80,261 (EX-99.1_2026-05-05_alks-ex99_1.htm.jsonl page:6), Q2 is 219,479 less 80,261 = 139,218 (EX-99.1_2026-07-28_alks-ex99_1.htm.jsonl page:7) and Q3 is 120,065 (EX-99.1_2026-11-03_alks-ex99_1.htm.jsonl page:6). 4. Total debt = current portion 26,500 + long-term debt 1,471,231 = 1,497,731 (10-Q_2026-09-30_alks-20260930.htm.jsonl page:6), which equals Term Loan A 735,016 + Term Loan B 762,715 (page:27). Cash and investments = 631,314 + 124,150 + 32,110 = 787,574 (pages:5-6). Net debt = 1,497,731 - 787,574 = 710,157. At December 31, 2025: debt nil; cash and investments 388,570 + 199,645 + 145 = 588,360 (10-K page:165), so net debt = -588,360. 5. Ratios. Total debt / LTM Adjusted EBITDA = 1,497,731 / 440,190 = 3.40x. Net debt / LTM Adjusted EBITDA = 710,157 / 440,190 = 1.61x. On principal 1,511,750: 3.43x and (1,511,750 - 787,574) / 440,190 = 1.65x. On LTM EBITDA 146,169: 1,497,731 / 146,169 = 10.25x and 710,157 / 146,169 = 4.86x. December 31, 2025: -588,360 / 394,304 = -1.49x (on EBITDA 285,588: -2.06x); including restricted cash of 731,206 the figure would be -1,319,566 / 394,304 = -3.35x. 6. LTM interest expense = 12,277 + 74,368 - nil = 86,645. Adjusted EBITDA / interest expense: LTM 440,190 / 86,645 = 5.08x; nine months 2026 339,544 / 74,368 = 4.57x; Q3 2026 120,065 / 27,551 = 4.36x. Reported EBITDA: LTM 146,169 / 86,645 = 1.69x; Q3 2026 62,960 / 27,551 = 2.29x. 7. Analyst estimate of Q3 2026 interest excluding one-offs: 27,551 less arranger fees 2,600 less write-off 500 less amortization of discount and fees 600 = 23,851 (amounts stated in millions in 10-Q page:29-30, so approximate); times four = 95,404; Q3 Adjusted EBITDA 120,065 / 23,851 = 5.03x. This is an estimate, not a reported figure. 8. LTM flows. Revenue 1,475,899 + 1,369,052 - 1,091,352 = 1,753,599. Product sales 1,184,643 + 1,167,118 - 869,151 = 1,482,610. Operating income 253,956 + 6,097 - 195,852 = 64,201. Net income 241,664 - 49,692 - 192,323 = -351. Cash from operations 520,754 + 72,917 - 350,685 = 242,986. Additions of PP&E 40,420 + 15,638 - 40,440 = 15,618. Free cash flow 242,986 - 15,618 = 227,368. Adjusted EBITDA margin on LTM revenue is 440,190 / 1,753,599 = 25.1%. 9. Discrete Q3 cash flows by subtraction (cumulative nine months less six months): cash from operations 72,917 - (-20,560) = 93,477 for 2026 and 350,685 - 249,013 = 101,672 for 2025; additions of PP&E 15,638 - 12,236 = 3,402 and 40,440 - 23,126 = 17,314; free cash flow 90,075 and 84,358 (10-Q Q2 page:7 and 10-Q Q3 page:7). Free cash flow FY2025 520,754 - 40,420 = 480,334; nine months 2026 72,917 - 15,638 = 57,279; nine months 2025 350,685 - 40,440 = 310,245. 10. Maturity table check: 6,625 + 26,500 + 40,563 + 45,250 + 45,250 + 1,347,562 = 1,511,750, equal to the printed total (10-Q Q3 page:29). Carrying 1,497,731 plus unamortized discount 10,400 plus fees 3,600 (millions rounded) = 1,511,731 against principal 1,511,750, a rounding difference of 19. 11. Cash and investments by quarter: March 31, 2026 351,551 + 160,311 + 26,363 = 538,225; June 30, 2026 511,529 + 145,048 + 35,054 = 691,631; both match the releases (EX-99.1_2026-05-05_alks-ex99_1.htm.jsonl page:6 and EX-99.1_2026-07-28_alks-ex99_1.htm.jsonl page:7). Debt carrying: March 31 26,500 + 1,483,837 = 1,510,337; June 30 26,500 + 1,476,611 = 1,503,111. 12. Quarterly Adjusted EBITDA add-back check: costs related to the acquisition of Avadel 55,825 (Q1) + 32,525 (88,350 less 55,825, Q2) + 29,790 (Q3) = 118,140, equal to the printed nine-month figure. Share-based compensation 54,581 + 31,296 + 26,747 = 112,624, equal to the nine-month figure; the cash flow statement shows 36,330, 31,139 (67,469 less 36,330) and 26,747, total 94,216, a difference of 18,408 as logged. 13. Collar notional 375,000 + 375,000 = 750,000; 750,000 / 1,511,750 = 49.6% of scheduled principal. 14. Lease liabilities at September 30, 2026: 7,590 + 65,760 = 73,350; at December 31, 2025: 6,746 + 63,253 = 69,999 (10-K page:192 prints 69,999).

facts.label: Business and transaction view
facts.text: Alkermes plc is an Irish-incorporated, Nasdaq-listed neuroscience company with U.S. commercial operations. Before 2026 its earnings came from three proprietary U.S. products (VIVITROL, ARISTADA and ARISTADA INITIO, LYBALVI) and from royalty and manufacturing revenue on long-acting antipsychotics sold by Janssen and on VUMERITY sold by Biogen. The Avadel Pharmaceuticals plc acquisition, completed on February 12, 2026, added LUMRYZ and its commercial organisation, was financed by senior secured term loans and balance sheet cash, and created a contingent value right that can add a further cash payment. The transaction is the dominant credit event in the pack: it moved the company from no debt at December 31, 2025 to senior secured term loans, it brought acquired intangibles and goodwill that make up most of the purchase price, and it changed the revenue mix toward a product distributed through a closed pharmacy network. The creditor-relevant business risks are concentration in a few products and three wholesalers, expected VIVITROL generic entry in 2027, patent challenges against LYBALVI and LUMRYZ, government rebate exposure, and reliance on the pipeline (alixorexton, ALKS 7290) for growth that the debt service does not depend on today. Mitigants documented in the pack are that ARISTADA patents run to 2039 and LYBALVI patents to 2041, that LUMRYZ has orphan drug exclusivity through May 1, 2030 for adults, that no dividends have been paid, and that the company reports cash and investments of 787.6 US$m at September 30, 2026 (from the CP-1 handoff). Ownership and board composition are Not supplied, so sponsor and control analysis is limited to documented corporate actions.

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: The Avadel Acquisition is the transaction for this run. In October 2025 the company and Avadel "entered into a definitive transaction agreement, subsequently amended in November 2025" (10-K_2025-12-31_alks-20251231.htm.jsonl page:10). The consideration is $21.00 per Avadel share in cash at closing plus a non-transferable contingent value right of $1.50 per share payable on a specified milestone (page:10). The acquisition closed on February 12, 2026 (10-Q_2026-09-30_alks-20260930.htm.jsonl page:15). Preliminary purchase consideration was 2,306.9 US$m, being 2,064.3 US$m for Avadel shares, 134.9 US$m cash settlement of equity awards and 107.7 US$m fair value of the CVR, so cash paid at closing was 2,199.2 US$m (page:16). The potential CVR payment totals $165.7 million (page:53), and management expects the milestone to be determined by the end of 2027 (page:53); the probability of success was raised from 75% to 90% after positive phase 3 results for LUMRYZ in idiopathic hypersomnia (page:24). The type is a strategic acquisition by a listed strategic buyer; there is no sponsor.

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: Financing and liquidity effect (CP-1 handoff figures). Before closing the company arranged a senior secured bridge facility of up to approximately $1.5 billion in November 2025 and placed approximately $731.2 million of its cash in escrow (10-K page:193). At closing it entered the credit agreement and borrowed the full $1.525 billion available under two term loans, which replaced the bridge. After the August 12, 2026 amendment the facilities carried 1,497.7 US$m (carrying) at September 30, 2026, Term Loan A due February 12, 2031 and Term Loan B due August 12, 2031, with margins of 1.75% to 2.25% and 2.25% over Term SOFR. No bond or note issuance appears in the debt note; the new debt is bank term debt only. Liquidity at September 30, 2026 was cash and investments of 787.6 US$m with no revolving facility found in the sources. The deal moved leverage from nil at December 31, 2025 to 3.40 times LTM Adjusted EBITDA (management measure with a derived FY2025 component), per the CP-1 handoff.

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: Use of proceeds and status. The term loan proceeds and the escrowed cash funded the cash consideration; the cash consideration of 2,199.2 US$m less net debt proceeds of 1,511.6 US$m leaves 687.7 US$m from cash, below the escrow, and the sources do not state what the remaining escrow was used for (this is arithmetic, not a sources and uses table). The purchase price allocation is preliminary and may be adjusted for up to one year from closing (page:16). Goodwill of 509.5 US$m and acquired intangible assets of 1,794.9 US$m were recognised at closing, so identifiable intangibles are most of the consideration, and if LUMRYZ underperforms the carrying values are exposed to impairment (Analyst Interpretation; no impairment is reported). The company states it cannot present Avadel's separate net income because the businesses "do not operate as discrete entities within the Company" after integration (page:19).

facts.label: Credit view
facts.text: Alkermes plc is a moderately leveraged specialty drug company whose secured term loans look serviceable from current cash flow, but whose coverage depends on managing expected VIVITROL generic entry in 2027 and on integrating LUMRYZ. The strongest support is liquidity: USD 787.6 million of cash and investments against USD 26.5 million of principal due in 2027 and only USD 164.2 million due before 2031. The weakest point is that total debt of USD 1,497.7 million is 3.40x LTM Adjusted EBITDA but 10.25x reported EBITDA, so leverage rests on management add-backs, and covenant levels cannot be read. The outcome will be decided by whether legacy cash flow is replaced as VIVITROL erodes, and by the covenant terms not yet supplied.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Alkermes borrowed its full USD 1,525.0 million of term loans to buy Avadel, moving from no debt at December 31, 2025 to USD 1,497.7 million of senior secured debt at September 30, 2026. The debt is two bank term loans with no bonds. Scheduled principal is USD 6.625 million for the rest of 2026, USD 26.500 million in 2027, USD 40.563 million in 2028 and USD 45.250 million in each of 2029 and 2030, which leaves 89.1% of principal due in 2031 (new arithmetic, see Calculations) [financial base: debt and capital structure]. Liquidity of USD 787.6 million of cash and investments, with no revolver found, is what the creditor can rely on, and it comfortably covers amortization.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Leverage is the central judgement. On LTM Adjusted EBITDA of USD 440.2 million, total debt is 3.40x and net debt 1.61x, but LTM reported EBITDA is only USD 146.2 million, which gives 10.25x and 4.86x. The difference is acquisition costs, inventory step-up, share-based compensation and a contingent consideration charge, and the FY2025 part of LTM Adjusted EBITDA is derived by the analyst. Expense-basis cover is 5.08x on Adjusted EBITDA, with cash interest unreported [financial base: leverage and coverage].

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Business risk is concentrated. VIVITROL was 31.7% of FY2025 revenue and generic entry is expected in 2027, while ARISTADA patents run to 2039 and LYBALVI patents to 2041, with LYBALVI facing paragraph IV challenges, and the legacy products rely on three wholesalers. LUMRYZ supplied 16.5% of nine-month 2026 revenue through four specialty pharmacies, bears a 3.85% royalty to Jazz and faces a generic challenge [business context: operating model and credit translations]. Cash from operations of USD 72.9 million for nine months 2026, against USD 350.7 million a year earlier, shows how heavily the first year of integration weighed on cash, while LTM free cash flow of USD 227.4 million shows the recovery to date [financial base: cash flow quality].

facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Strengths. (1) Liquidity and maturity profile: USD 787.6 million of cash and investments against light amortization and a 2031-weighted maturity wall, which gives time to absorb the 2027 VIVITROL change (Documentary Fact; financial base). (2) Cash generation: LTM free cash flow of USD 227.4 million with low capital spending, equal to 15.2% of debt (Documentary Fact for the inputs; the ratio is Analyst Interpretation). (3) Portfolio breadth beyond one product: four proprietary products plus royalties, with ARISTADA patents to 2039, LYBALVI to 2041 and LUMRYZ orphan exclusivity to 2030 for adults (Documentary Fact; business context). (4) Interest rate protection on USD 750.0 million of notional through collars entered in October 2026, though covenant effects are unknown (Documentary Fact). (5) Documented financial behaviour has been conservative: debt prepaid in 2024, no dividends, no buybacks in Q2 or Q3 2026 (Documentary Fact; Analyst Interpretation on what it implies).

facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Weaknesses. (1) Dependence on add-backs: 3.40x on Adjusted EBITDA against 10.25x on reported EBITDA, with a derived FY2025 base and share-based compensation add-backs that do not tie to the statements (Documentary Fact; the dependence is Analyst Interpretation). (2) Product concentration and generic risk: VIVITROL at 31.7% of FY2025 revenue with generic entry expected in 2027, and product-level margins Not supplied, so the cash flow effect cannot be sized (Documentary Fact; Insufficient Information for the effect). (3) Secured structure without visible covenants: all debt is secured on substantially all assets, but levels, definitions and the margin grid are Not supplied, and Term Loan B is outside the maintenance tests (Insufficient Information). (4) Floating-rate exposure: Term SOFR plus 1.75% to 2.25% on Term Loan A and 2.25% on Term Loan B, half of principal hedged by collars (Documentary Fact; the share is arithmetic). (5) Acquisition accounting and contingent liability: a preliminary purchase price allocation, intangibles and goodwill that make up most of the consideration, and a possible payment of USD 165.7 million carried at USD 136.9 million (Documentary Fact; the impairment exposure is Analyst Interpretation). (6) Channel and counterparty concentration: three wholesalers for legacy products and four specialty pharmacies for LUMRYZ (Documentary Fact). (7) Thin interim cash conversion: nine-month 2026 cash from operations of USD 72.9 million (Documentary Fact).

## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| The filed statements and earnings releases through the third quarter of 2026 support a credit snapshot of Alkermes after the Avadel acquisition, with limitations. Debt, cash and operating results are well covered; covenant levels are not. | Medium | The credit agreement and its amendment are not in the pack, so covenant levels, guarantors and pricing grid cannot be read. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |
| Audited FY2025 statements and three 2026 quarterly reports are present, with matching earnings releases. | Annual and quarterly figures can be traced to filed statements. | High |
| The Avadel acquisition closed on February 12, 2026, so 2026 periods are not comparable with FY2025. | Pre-acquisition history understates the current debt and cost base. | High |
| Debt is two term loans with carrying and principal amounts in the notes; covenant levels are only named. | Leverage and coverage headroom cannot be tested from the pack. | Medium |
| No revolving facility, interest paid for 2026 or rating is found in the sources. | Liquidity rests on cash and investments only. | Medium |
| The purchase price allocation is preliminary and some management add-backs differ from statement figures. | Goodwill, intangibles and adjusted EBITDA may be restated or need care. | Medium |
### Readiness view

The effective source set is READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS for the four downstream modules that CP-OS will run. The pack contains the audited FY2025 annual report, the three 2026 quarterly reports including the quarter ended September 30, 2026 filed before the cutoff, and the three matching earnings releases, so statements, debt and liquidity notes, the Avadel business combination note, litigation, subsequent events and management non-GAAP reconciliations are all located in filed or furnished text. The limiting gaps are source gaps, not extraction failures: the executed credit agreement and its first amendment are referenced but not supplied, so covenant levels, step-downs, the margin grid, guarantor identities and baskets cannot be read; no revolving credit facility is described anywhere in the pack; cash paid for interest is not presented for any 2026 period; the Avadel purchase price allocation is preliminary; no presentation decks are supplied; and the discrete fourth quarter of 2025 has no standalone report. None of these prevents a consumer from performing its own method, because each consumer can state the gap and carry it forward. No consumer is CONDITIONAL or BLOCKED. The next evidence action is to obtain the executed credit agreement and amendment (both listed as exhibits) before any covenant headroom is stated.
### Source-by-source assessment
| Source | Original authority and perimeter | Period and basis | Version relationship and limitation |

| 10-K FY2025 | Audited annual report of Alkermes plc and subsidiaries; auditor opinion present on page:162 and statements on pages:165-168 | Years ended December 31, 2025, 2024 and 2023, USD thousands, US GAAP | Pre-acquisition: Avadel acquisition and the term loans are described as post-year-end events. Authority for FY2025; superseded for 2026 by later 10-Qs |

| 10-Q Q1 2026 | Unaudited condensed consolidated statements of Alkermes plc and subsidiaries | Three months ended March 31, 2026 versus 2025 and December 31, 2025 balance sheet | First report including Avadel (closed February 12, 2026) and the original term loans; amounts later affected by the August 2026 amendment |
| 10-Q Q2 2026 | Unaudited condensed consolidated | Three and six months ended June 30, 2026 | Separate active source; cumulative six-month cash flow, not discrete Q2 |

| 10-Q Q3 2026 | Unaudited condensed consolidated; most recent filing, signed November 3, 2026 | Three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 | Controls Q3 2026 and the September 30, 2026 balance sheet; describes the amended credit agreement |
| EX-99.1 May 5, 2026 | Issuer earnings release; management narrative and non-GAAP | Q1 2026 | Supporting attributed claims; filings control where they differ |
| EX-99.1 July 28, 2026 | Issuer earnings release containing 2026 financial expectations | Q2 2026 | Contains the guidance table that the November release says it reiterates |

| EX-99.1 November 3, 2026 | Issuer earnings release, unaudited, with GAAP to Adjusted EBITDA reconciliation | Q3 2026 and nine months 2026 | The release states the 10-Q was still to be filed; the 10-Q in the pack is dated November 3, 2026 |

Entity roles. Alkermes plc is the registrant and the TopCo Borrower; Alkermes, Inc. is the U.S. Borrower and Alkermes Finance LLC the U.S. Co-Borrower (10-Q_2026-09-30_alks-20260930.htm.jsonl page:28, "Alkermes plc, as the TopCo Borrower, Alkermes, Inc., as the U.S. Borrower, Alkermes Finance LLC, as the U.S. Co-Borrower"). Guarantors are only described generically: "The Credit Agreement is guaranteed by subsidiary guarantors and secured by a lien on substantially all of the assets of the borrowers and the subsidiary guarantors" (10-Q_2026-09-30_alks-20260930.htm.jsonl page:28). No parent, sponsor, restricted or unrestricted subsidiary designation appears in the pack or the context; the registrant is the top entity and listed equity issuer. Presentation is consolidated and single-segment: "is managed as one segment on a consolidated basis" (10-Q_2026-09-30_alks-20260930.htm.jsonl page:14).
### Coverage by evidence area
| Evidence area | Located evidence | Status |

| Audited annual statements | Audit opinion: "present fairly, in all material respects, the financial position of the Company as of December 31, 2025 and 2024" (10-K_2025-12-31_alks-20251231.htm.jsonl page:162); balance sheet page:165, operations page:166, cash flows page:168 | Retained |

| Subsequent events to cutoff | October 2026 interest rate collars: "In October 2026, the Company entered into two zero-cost interest rate collar agreements, each with a notional amount of $375.0 million" (10-Q_2026-09-30_alks-20260930.htm.jsonl page:30) | Retained |
### Strongest contrary evidence and limitations

1. Covenants. The covenant package is named but not quantified: "requires the maintenance of a maximum Secured Net Leverage Ratio and a minimum Consolidated Interest Coverage Ratio (as defined in the Credit Agreement), in each case, with the levels set forth in the Credit Agreement" (10-Q_2026-09-30_alks-20260930.htm.jsonl page:28), and compliance is a management statement only: "The Company was in compliance with its debt covenants at September 30, 2026." (page:30). The text carves out the Term Loan B from the maintenance tests. Mechanism: without levels, defined terms and add-back rules, headroom cannot be computed from the statements, so any leverage or coverage view is a computed ratio, not the covenant measure.

2. Period comparability. The business combination closed on February 12, 2026, so nine months 2026 contains Avadel results only from that date, while FY2025 and nine months 2025 contain none. The company states that "the presentation of net (loss) income is impracticable due to the integration of Avadel’s operations" (10-Q_2026-09-30_alks-20260930.htm.jsonl page:19). Unaudited pro forma revenue and net income are given in the same note, as a separate comparative basis. Consequence: trend statements across FY2025 and 2026 need the pro forma note and explicit labelling.

3. Preliminary accounting. "The Company’s purchase price allocation is preliminary" (10-Q_2026-09-30_alks-20260930.htm.jsonl page:16, in the note text "purchase price allocation is preliminary and based on the information available as of the reporting date"); goodwill and intangibles can still move for up to one year from closing.

4. Liquidity structure. No revolving facility, undrawn commitment or letter of credit facility is described in any pinned source (searches for "revolv" returned no match in all seven sources). The only letters of credit mentioned are collateralised by held-to-maturity investments tied to leases (10-Q_2026-09-30_alks-20260930.htm.jsonl page:50). Liquidity therefore equals cash and investments in the sources, and the absence of a revolver is a finding of the searched text, not proof the issuer has none.

5. Management add-backs. The nine-month reconciliation adds back share-based compensation of 112,624 thousand (EX-99.1_2026-11-03_alks-ex99_1.htm.jsonl page:6) while the cash flow statement shows 94,216 thousand (10-Q_2026-09-30_alks-20260930.htm.jsonl page:7). The difference is unexplained in the pack and is carried as a conflict below.

Source-check arithmetic is in Calculations |

| Share-based compensation, Q3 2026 | 26,747 thousand in the release (EX-99.1_2026-11-03_alks-ex99_1.htm.jsonl page:6) | 27,308 thousand in the equity statement (10-Q_2026-09-30_alks-20260930.htm.jsonl page:8) | Same as above, quarter basis |

| Balance sheet captions | Release shows Other assets of 152,604 thousand (EX-99.1_2026-11-03_alks-ex99_1.htm.jsonl page:7) | 10-Q shows Other assets of 72,876 thousand and right-of-use assets of 79,728 thousand (10-Q_2026-09-30_alks-20260930.htm.jsonl pages:5-6) | Classification difference between release and 10-Q; filed 10-Q controls |
### Consumer readiness
| Consumer | Assessment | Evidence demand and carried limitation |

| CP-1 (financial extraction and credit metrics) | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Needs statements, debt table, maturities, cash flow and non-GAAP. All present. Carry: no covenant levels, no revolver, no 2026 cash interest paid, preliminary allocation, Avadel comparability, SBC add-back differences. Discrete Q4 2025 has no standalone report; annual FY2025 plus nine-month comparatives are present |

| CP-1A (business and transaction context) | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Needs business description, Avadel transaction terms, milestone payment, litigation and history. Present in the 10-K Item 1 and 10-Q notes. Carry: the Avadel transaction agreement and CVR terms are exhibits not supplied; management language in releases is attributed, not adopted |

| CP-2 (fundamental credit synthesis) | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Draws only on CP-1 and CP-1A handoffs, which the dependency planner sequences; no source condition. Carry all CP-1 and CP-1A gaps, plus no ratings or market data in the context |

Extraction fidelity. All seven sources extracted to page text. Extraction is not a fidelity review: tables are flattened so each number sits on its own line, which preserves values but not layout. No images, charts or speaker notes were inspected, and no deck is supplied, so no presentation coverage is claimed. The November release mentions "webcast presentation with accompanying slides" (EX-99.1_2026-11-03_alks-ex99_1.htm.jsonl page:2), and those slides are not in the pack.
## Calculations

No normalization, reconciliation or new analytical figure is produced in this module. The following source-consistency checks use only printed figures and are recorded so downstream modules know which ties hold.

The scheduled 2026 remaining payment is 6,625 thousand, which is close but is not asserted as the cause |

| Borrowing flows | Net proceeds on original borrowings 1,511.6 million plus 45.5 million additional proceeds equals 1,557.1 million, matching proceeds from issuance of debt, net of 1,557,097 thousand (10-Q_2026-09-30_alks-20260930.htm.jsonl pages:7 and 52) | Ties |

### Financial base view

The financial base is adequate for a credit snapshot of the post-acquisition Alkermes, with the limits stated here. Before February 12, 2026 the company was unlevered: no debt at December 31, 2025, 388.6 US$m of cash and equivalents, 199.8 US$m of investments and 731.2 US$m of restricted cash held in escrow for the Avadel acquisition. The acquisition cost 2,199.2 US$m in cash plus a contingent value right, funded by 1,525.0 US$m of term loans (net proceeds 1,511.6 US$m) and balance sheet cash. At September 30, 2026 the balance sheet carries 1,497.7 US$m of term loan debt (net of 14.0 US$m of discount and fees), 787.6 US$m of cash and investments and no restricted cash. LTM revenue is 1,753.6 US$m against 1,475.9 US$m in FY2025, mostly from the addition of LUMRYZ. GAAP profit is near zero over the LTM because of inventory step-up amortization, acquisition costs, intangible amortization, a contingent consideration fair value charge and 86.6 US$m of interest expense, and the management measures are the main bridge to leverage. On the management Adjusted EBITDA basis, total debt is 3.40 times LTM and net debt 1.61 times; on the company-definition reported EBITDA the same ratios are 10.25 and 4.86 times. The covenant package, the margin grid and any revolver are not readable from the pack, so headroom, undrawn liquidity and cash coverage are Not supplied. Debt service is modest through 2030 (scheduled amortization of 6.6 to 45.3 US$m a year) with nearly all principal due in 2031, which places the refinancing test in 2031.
### Reporting entity, periods and definitions

The reporting entity is Alkermes plc and subsidiaries, consolidated, US GAAP, USD thousands, one reportable segment ("is managed as one segment on a consolidated basis", 10-Q_2026-09-30_alks-20260930.htm.jsonl page:14). The borrowers are Alkermes plc (TopCo Borrower), Alkermes, Inc. (U.S. Borrower) and Alkermes Finance LLC (U.S. Co-Borrower); guarantors are unnamed (10-Q_2026-09-30_alks-20260930.htm.jsonl page:28).

Period labels used throughout: FY2025 is the year ended December 31, 2025 (audited). Nine months 2026 and 2025 are the cumulative periods ended September 30. Q3 2026 and Q3 2025 are the three months ended September 30. LTM Sep 30, 2026 is FY2025 plus nine months 2026 less nine months 2025. Discrete Q3 cash flow figures are the nine-month amount less the six-month amount because the 10-Qs print cumulative cash flows.

EBITDA definitions. Reported EBITDA is the company measure: "EBITDA represents earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortization." (EX-99.1_2026-11-03_alks-ex99_1.htm.jsonl page:3), reconciled from net income by deducting interest income and adding interest expense, tax, depreciation and amortization of acquired intangibles (page:6). Adjusted EBITDA is management's measure: "Adjusted EBITDA excludes share-based compensation expense and non-recurring gains or losses in addition to the components of EBITDA from earnings." (page:3). For nine months 2026 the add-backs are share-based compensation of 112.6 US$m, costs related to the acquisition of Avadel of 118.1 US$m and the contingent consideration fair value change of 27.0 US$m (page:6). Neither measure is a covenant measure; the credit agreement defines Secured Net Leverage Ratio and Consolidated Interest Coverage Ratio, and those definitions are Not supplied. Total debt in this handoff is the balance sheet carrying amount of the term loans (current portion plus long-term debt); net debt deducts cash and equivalents plus short-term and long-term investments, which are not restricted. Operating leases, the contingent consideration and the litigation matters are outside the debt figure.
### Reported results

Q3 2026 total revenues were 480.1 US$m against 394.2 US$m in Q3 2025, with product sales net of 417.3 US$m against 317.4 US$m (10-Q_2026-09-30_alks-20260930.htm.jsonl page:6). The 10-Q attributes the increase "primarily due to the addition of LUMRYZ to our proprietary product portfolio" (page:37). The release shows LUMRYZ net sales of 89.9 US$m for Q3 2026 and 226.0 US$m for nine months 2026, with no comparative because the product was acquired (EX-99.1_2026-11-03_alks-ex99_1.htm.jsonl page:1). Manufacturing and royalty revenues fell to 62.9 US$m in Q3 2026 from 76.8 US$m in Q3 2025 (10-Q_2026-09-30_alks-20260930.htm.jsonl page:6), and LYBALVI net sales slipped to 95.9 US$m from 98.2 US$m (EX-99.1_2026-11-03_alks-ex99_1.htm.jsonl page:1). Q3 2026 operating income was 36.0 US$m against 89.1 US$m, and GAAP net income was 16.3 US$m against 82.8 US$m, with interest expense of 27.6 US$m against nil (page:6-7). Nine months 2026 shows an operating income of 6.1 US$m and a net loss of 49.7 US$m. Quarterly Adjusted EBITDA was 80.3 US$m in Q1 2026, 139.2 US$m in Q2 2026 and 120.1 US$m in Q3 2026 (derived from the cumulative reconciliations; see Calculations), against 121.5 US$m in Q3 2025. Management reiterated its 2026 expectations in November (EX-99.1_2026-11-03_alks-ex99_1.htm.jsonl page:2); the July release sets out projected 2026 Adjusted EBITDA of 390.0 US$m at the mid-point of ranges (EX-99.1_2026-07-28_alks-ex99_1.htm.jsonl page:8), which is management guidance, not evidence.
### Debt and capital structure

At September 30, 2026 the debt consists of two senior secured term loans under the February 12, 2026 credit agreement, as amended by Amendment No. 1 on August 12, 2026: Term Loan A Facility due February 12, 2031 at a carrying amount of 735.0 US$m and Term Loan B Facility due August 12, 2031 at 762.7 US$m, total 1,497.7 US$m, of which 26.5 US$m is current (10-Q_2026-09-30_alks-20260930.htm.jsonl pages:6 and 27). Scheduled principal is 1,511.75 US$m, and the company states "At September 30, 2026, our borrowings consisted of $1.511 billion outstanding under the Facilities." (page:55). Unamortized discount and fees are "$3.6 million and $10.4 million, respectively" (page:30). The facilities were drawn in full at closing at 1,525.0 US$m: "the Company borrowed the full $1.525 billion available under the Facilities" (10-K_2025-12-31_alks-20251231.htm.jsonl page:193). Pricing after the amendment is Term SOFR plus 1.75% to 2.25% on Term Loan A, set by a Secured Net Leverage Ratio grid that is not supplied, and Term SOFR plus 2.25% on Term Loan B; the amendment cut the spread by 0.75% on Term Loan A and 0.50% on Term Loan B (page:28). The original margin was 2.75% on both (10-Q_2026-03-31_alks-20260331.htm.jsonl page:23). Three-month SOFR was 4.07% at September 30, 2026, and the company estimates that a 10% rise in the rate would raise interest from October 1 to December 31, 2026 by $1.6 million (10-Q_2026-09-30_alks-20260930.htm.jsonl page:55).

The Facilities are "guaranteed by subsidiary guarantors and secured by a lien on substantially all of the assets of the borrowers and the subsidiary guarantors" (page:28). All debt therefore ranks as senior secured with no unsecured or subordinated tranche; no other debt instrument appears in the debt note. The amendment was accounted for lender by lender, with three exiting Term Loan B lenders treated as extinguished and one new lender as new issuance (page:29), with a 0.5 US$m write-off of deferred costs and 2.6 US$m of arranger fees in Q3 interest expense.

Maturity wall (scheduled principal, US$m, from the table at page:29): remaining 2026 6.625; 2027 26.500; 2028 40.563; 2029 45.250; 2030 45.250; thereafter 1,347.562, total 1,511.750. Both facilities mature in 2031, so the thereafter amount falls in 2031 (inferred from the stated maturity dates). The wall is back-ended: the 2031 maturities represent most of the principal, and Term Loan B matures on August 12, 2031, six months after Term Loan A.

Hedging. In October 2026, after the balance sheet date and before the cutoff, "the Company entered into two zero-cost interest rate collar agreements, each with a notional amount of $375.0 million" with a Term SOFR cap of 5.25% and floors of 4.25% and 4.30%, maturing February 2029 and February 2030 (page:30). The notional total of 750.0 US$m covers about half of the principal.

Claims outside the debt figure. (1) Operating leases: lease liabilities of 7.6 US$m current and 65.8 US$m long-term at September 30, 2026 (page:6); all leases are operating leases (10-K_2025-12-31_alks-20251231.htm.jsonl page:192) and the 10-Q reports "Cash paid for lease liabilities was $2.9 million and $8.6 million during the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026" (10-Q_2026-09-30_alks-20260930.htm.jsonl page:27). (2) Contingent consideration: the CVR entitles former Avadel holders to "a potential additional aggregate cash payment of $165.7 million, or $1.50 per Avadel Share, upon achievement of the CVR Milestone" (page:53), carried at 136.9 US$m on the balance sheet (page:6) against 107.7 US$m at the acquisition date (page:16); management expects the milestone to be determined by the end of 2027 (page:53) and raised the probability of success from 75% to 90% after positive LUMRYZ phase 3 results in idiopathic hypersomnia (page:24). (3) Capital commitments: open purchase orders were $17.7 million at December 31, 2025 (10-K_2025-12-31_alks-20251231.htm.jsonl page:212); the 10-Q does not update this. (4) Litigation: the company states no probable material losses at September 30, 2026 and that no range can be estimated for reasonably possible claims (10-Q_2026-09-30_alks-20260930.htm.jsonl page:34); the Acorda matter, a petition seeking about $66.0 million of additional damages, was decided in the company's favour by the Second Circuit on July 15, 2026 and Acorda filed a certiorari petition on October 13, 2026 (page:36). (5) Pensions, factoring and supply chain finance: no pension, factoring or supply chain finance arrangement was found in the 10-K or the September 10-Q text (searches returned no match), so these are Not supplied rather than nil.
### Liquidity

Liquidity at September 30, 2026 is cash and cash equivalents of 631.3 US$m plus short-term investments of 124.2 US$m and long-term investments of 32.1 US$m, total 787.6 US$m, which the release states as "$787.6 million" (EX-99.1_2026-11-03_alks-ex99_1.htm.jsonl page:2). No revolving facility, undrawn committed facility or letter of credit line is described in any pinned source, so undrawn committed facilities are Not supplied and available liquidity is cash and investments only; this is the finding of the searched text and not proof that none exists. The only letters of credit mentioned are collateralised by held-to-maturity investments tied to leases (10-Q_2026-09-30_alks-20260930.htm.jsonl page:50). Cash fell to 351.6 US$m at March 31, 2026 as the acquisition closed and the escrow was used, then rose to 511.5 US$m at June 30 and 631.3 US$m at September 30. Management states: "We expect that our existing cash, cash equivalents and investments will be sufficient to finance our anticipated working capital and other cash requirements" (page:50). Near-term debt service is the 26.5 US$m current portion and interest; no facility expires within twelve months.
### Cash flow quality

Cash flow from operations was 72.9 US$m for nine months 2026 against 350.7 US$m for nine months 2025 (10-Q_2026-09-30_alks-20260930.htm.jsonl page:7). The 2026 figure is after a net loss of 49.7 US$m, add-backs of 94.2 US$m share-based compensation, 76.9 US$m depreciation and amortization, 72.4 US$m inventory step-up amortization and 27.0 US$m contingent consideration fair value, and a working capital outflow of 156.8 US$m (page:51), including a 116.4 US$m outflow in accounts payable and accrued expenses (page:7). Capital expenditure was low at 15.6 US$m. Cash taxes paid were 34.9 US$m against 3.1 US$m (page:8). Free cash flow, defined here as cash from operations less additions of property, plant and equipment, was 57.3 US$m for nine months 2026 and 227.4 US$m over the LTM, against 480.3 US$m in FY2025. Q3 2026 alone generated 93.5 US$m of operating cash flow (derived by subtraction), which suggests recovery after the heavy first half, but one quarter is not a trend. Share-based compensation is large relative to Adjusted EBITDA: the release adds back 112.6 US$m of it in nine months 2026 against Adjusted EBITDA of 339.5 US$m. It is a non-cash but recurring cost, and the sources do not say whether it is settled in cash.
### Leverage and coverage

Leverage. On total debt of 1,497.7 US$m (carrying) and LTM Adjusted EBITDA of 440.2 US$m (derived, see below), total debt to EBITDA is 3.40 times; net debt of 710.2 US$m gives 1.61 times. On principal of 1,511.75 US$m the ratios are 3.43 and 1.65 times. On LTM reported EBITDA of 146.2 US$m the ratios are 10.25 and 4.86 times. The gap between the bases is explained by add-backs of acquisition-related costs, share-based compensation and the inventory step-up that flows through cost of goods sold; the step-up is non-cash and, as an analyst inference, should roll off as the acquired inventory is sold, whereas share-based compensation is a recurring cost. At December 31, 2025 there was no debt; net debt was negative 588.4 US$m (cash 388.6 plus investments 199.8), and 731.2 US$m of restricted cash is excluded from that figure.

Coverage. Cash paid for interest is not presented for any 2026 period (the supplemental cash flow disclosure shows taxes only), and the 10-K shows cash paid for interest of nil in FY2025, so EBITDA to cash interest is Not supplied. On an expense basis, Q3 2026 Adjusted EBITDA of 120.1 US$m covers interest expense of 27.6 US$m 4.36 times, nine months 4.57 times, and LTM 5.08 times; reported EBITDA covers interest expense 2.29 times in Q3 2026 and 1.69 times over the LTM. Interest expense includes non-cash and one-off items: 7.4 US$m of bridge facility financing costs in the nine months, 2.6 US$m of arranger fees and 0.5 US$m of deferred cost write-off in Q3, and amortization of discount and fees of 0.6 US$m in Q3. An analyst estimate that removes the Q3 items gives about 23.9 US$m for the quarter, an annualised 95.4 US$m, but this is an estimate, not a reported figure.
### Latest quarter and events to the cutoff

Q3 2026 events: Amendment No. 1 to the credit agreement on August 12, 2026 reduced spreads and re-cut lender allocations, with 45.5 US$m of additional borrowings and 45.5 US$m of repayments to exiting lenders in financing cash flow (10-Q_2026-09-30_alks-20260930.htm.jsonl page:52); a new LUMRYZ patent suit against Granules India Limited was filed on July 30, 2026 (page:35); the Value Drug Company antitrust complaint on VIVITROL was partly dismissed on September 24, 2026 (page:36); and Blair Jackson was announced to assume the chief executive role on August 1, 2026 (EX-99.1_2026-07-28_alks-ex99_1.htm.jsonl page:1), the November release quoting him as President and Chief Executive Officer. Subsequent to the balance sheet date and before the cutoff: the October 2026 collars (above) and the Acorda certiorari petition on October 13, 2026. The Q3 10-Q was signed on November 3, 2026. No event after the cutoff is used.

## Calculations
All inputs are USD thousands as printed; results are in USD thousands unless stated. Locators are page numbers of the pinned sources.

1. FY2025 EBITDA (company definition, derived). Net income 241,664 less interest income 45,304 plus interest expense 12,277 plus income tax provision 49,786 plus depreciation and amortization 27,165 = 285,588 (10-K_2025-12-31_alks-20251231.htm.jsonl pages:166 and 168). The same method reproduces the printed nine-month 2025 EBITDA: 192,323 less 33,174 plus nil plus 38,750 plus 23,319 = 221,218 against 221,217 printed (rounding).

2. FY2025 Adjusted EBITDA (derived, approximate). EBITDA 285,588 plus share-based compensation 98,716 (10-K page:168) plus Avadel acquisition costs of "approximately $10.0 million" incurred in the fourth quarter of 2025 (10-K page:130, stated in millions) = 394,304. Nine-month 2025 Adjusted EBITDA of 293,658 equals EBITDA 221,217 plus share-based compensation 72,441 with no acquisition costs, so the only 2025 add-backs through September were share-based compensation. Implied Q4 2025 Adjusted EBITDA is 394,304 less 293,658 = 100,646. The approximation lies in the 10.0 US$m rounded cost and in whether the company would add back exactly that amount.

4. Total debt = current portion 26,500 + long-term debt 1,471,231 = 1,497,731 (10-Q_2026-09-30_alks-20260930.htm.jsonl page:6), which equals Term Loan A 735,016 + Term Loan B 762,715 (page:27). Cash and investments = 631,314 + 124,150 + 32,110 = 787,574 (pages:5-6). Net debt = 1,497,731 - 787,574 = 710,157. At December 31, 2025: debt nil; cash and investments 388,570 + 199,645 + 145 = 588,360 (10-K page:165), so net debt = -588,360.

7. Analyst estimate of Q3 2026 interest excluding one-offs: 27,551 less arranger fees 2,600 less write-off 500 less amortization of discount and fees 600 = 23,851 (amounts stated in millions in 10-Q page:29-30, so approximate); times four = 95,404; Q3 Adjusted EBITDA 120,065 / 23,851 = 5.03x. This is an estimate, not a reported figure.

9. Discrete Q3 cash flows by subtraction (cumulative nine months less six months): cash from operations 72,917 - (-20,560) = 93,477 for 2026 and 350,685 - 249,013 = 101,672 for 2025; additions of PP&E 15,638 - 12,236 = 3,402 and 40,440 - 23,126 = 17,314; free cash flow 90,075 and 84,358 (10-Q Q2 page:7 and 10-Q Q3 page:7). Free cash flow FY2025 520,754 - 40,420 = 480,334; nine months 2026 72,917 - 15,638 = 57,279; nine months 2025 350,685 - 40,440 = 310,245.

10. Maturity table check: 6,625 + 26,500 + 40,563 + 45,250 + 45,250 + 1,347,562 = 1,511,750, equal to the printed total (10-Q Q3 page:29). Carrying 1,497,731 plus unamortized discount 10,400 plus fees 3,600 (millions rounded) = 1,511,731 against principal 1,511,750, a rounding difference of 19.

12. Quarterly Adjusted EBITDA add-back check: costs related to the acquisition of Avadel 55,825 (Q1) + 32,525 (88,350 less 55,825, Q2) + 29,790 (Q3) = 118,140, equal to the printed nine-month figure. Share-based compensation 54,581 + 31,296 + 26,747 = 112,624, equal to the nine-month figure; the cash flow statement shows 36,330, 31,139 (67,469 less 36,330) and 26,747, total 94,216, a difference of 18,408 as logged.
13. Collar notional 375,000 + 375,000 = 750,000; 750,000 / 1,511,750 = 49.6% of scheduled principal.

### Business and transaction view

Alkermes plc is an Irish-incorporated, Nasdaq-listed neuroscience company with U.S. commercial operations. Before 2026 its earnings came from three proprietary U.S. products (VIVITROL, ARISTADA and ARISTADA INITIO, LYBALVI) and from royalty and manufacturing revenue on long-acting antipsychotics sold by Janssen and on VUMERITY sold by Biogen. The Avadel Pharmaceuticals plc acquisition, completed on February 12, 2026, added LUMRYZ and its commercial organisation, was financed by senior secured term loans and balance sheet cash, and created a contingent value right that can add a further cash payment. The transaction is the dominant credit event in the pack: it moved the company from no debt at December 31, 2025 to senior secured term loans, it brought acquired intangibles and goodwill that make up most of the purchase price, and it changed the revenue mix toward a product distributed through a closed pharmacy network. The creditor-relevant business risks are concentration in a few products and three wholesalers, expected VIVITROL generic entry in 2027, patent challenges against LYBALVI and LUMRYZ, government rebate exposure, and reliance on the pipeline (alixorexton, ALKS 7290) for growth that the debt service does not depend on today. Mitigants documented in the pack are that ARISTADA patents run to 2039 and LYBALVI patents to 2041, that LUMRYZ has orphan drug exclusivity through May 1, 2030 for adults, that no dividends have been paid, and that the company reports cash and investments of 787.6 US$m at September 30, 2026 (from the CP-1 handoff). Ownership and board composition are Not supplied, so sponsor and control analysis is limited to documented corporate actions.

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

The Avadel Acquisition is the transaction for this run. In October 2025 the company and Avadel "entered into a definitive transaction agreement, subsequently amended in November 2025" (10-K_2025-12-31_alks-20251231.htm.jsonl page:10). The consideration is $21.00 per Avadel share in cash at closing plus a non-transferable contingent value right of $1.50 per share payable on a specified milestone (page:10). The acquisition closed on February 12, 2026 (10-Q_2026-09-30_alks-20260930.htm.jsonl page:15). Preliminary purchase consideration was 2,306.9 US$m, being 2,064.3 US$m for Avadel shares, 134.9 US$m cash settlement of equity awards and 107.7 US$m fair value of the CVR, so cash paid at closing was 2,199.2 US$m (page:16). The potential CVR payment totals $165.7 million (page:53), and management expects the milestone to be determined by the end of 2027 (page:53); the probability of success was raised from 75% to 90% after positive phase 3 results for LUMRYZ in idiopathic hypersomnia (page:24). The type is a strategic acquisition by a listed strategic buyer; there is no sponsor.

Financing and liquidity effect (CP-1 handoff figures). Before closing the company arranged a senior secured bridge facility of up to approximately $1.5 billion in November 2025 and placed approximately $731.2 million of its cash in escrow (10-K page:193). At closing it entered the credit agreement and borrowed the full $1.525 billion available under two term loans, which replaced the bridge. After the August 12, 2026 amendment the facilities carried 1,497.7 US$m (carrying) at September 30, 2026, Term Loan A due February 12, 2031 and Term Loan B due August 12, 2031, with margins of 1.75% to 2.25% and 2.25% over Term SOFR. No bond or note issuance appears in the debt note; the new debt is bank term debt only. Liquidity at September 30, 2026 was cash and investments of 787.6 US$m with no revolving facility found in the sources. The deal moved leverage from nil at December 31, 2025 to 3.40 times LTM Adjusted EBITDA (management measure with a derived FY2025 component), per the CP-1 handoff.

Use of proceeds and status. The term loan proceeds and the escrowed cash funded the cash consideration; the cash consideration of 2,199.2 US$m less net debt proceeds of 1,511.6 US$m leaves 687.7 US$m from cash, below the escrow, and the sources do not state what the remaining escrow was used for (this is arithmetic, not a sources and uses table). The purchase price allocation is preliminary and may be adjusted for up to one year from closing (page:16). Goodwill of 509.5 US$m and acquired intangible assets of 1,794.9 US$m were recognised at closing, so identifiable intangibles are most of the consideration, and if LUMRYZ underperforms the carrying values are exposed to impairment (Analyst Interpretation; no impairment is reported). The company states it cannot present Avadel's separate net income because the businesses "do not operate as discrete entities within the Company" after integration (page:19).

Executed documents are listed as exhibits but not supplied: the Transaction Agreement and its amendment, the Credit Agreement and Amendment No. 1 (10-Q_2026-09-30_alks-20260930.htm.jsonl page:58; 10-Q_2026-03-31_alks-20260331.htm.jsonl page:50). Terms such as the CVR milestone definition, covenant levels and guarantor names are therefore Not supplied. Subsequent to the balance sheet date and before the cutoff, in October 2026 the company entered into two interest rate collars with a total notional of 750.0 US$m (CP-1 handoff; 10-Q page:30).

Fundamental credit synthesis for Alkermes plc. as of 2026-11-05, pathway credit_snapshot, current period Q3 2026 and prior period FY2025, in USD. It draws only on the three upstream handoffs (source readiness, financial base, business and transaction context), so no source text is read or quoted here and every figure is a value from the financial base handoff.
## Sources
### Issuer sources relied on (through the handoffs only)
| Source (exact name) | sha256 |
| 10-Q_2026-03-31_alks-20260331.htm.jsonl | 2f002a6c3ee21ba1a12ed08afd7616a7de0cb6e62154bfb1ecb118ba4eafd45f |
Run context (not issuer evidence): context sha256 885addee0d736fc42d87bc797174ed4ac35a16798074c06e23b1959b2f8975fb.
### Supplied handoffs
| Module | sha256 | Use |
| CP-0 | 1c390a89aa7513afef7abe9931b091489b79fa424d2c8a557db08f15d5e4f8c2 | Source readiness, gaps and conflicts (rated READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS) |
| CP-1 | ba17ec3b21ea8b787a38b6115fd45721db003c4757249d4451fa745fd7eb5b34 | Financial figures, debt, liquidity, leverage, cash flow |
| CP-1A | fb57077c42cf725224dc0c8dd52e411550d0fe38c0bf9122107c7138f80a50f8 | Business rows, transaction facts, governance, credit translations |
## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| Alkermes looks serviceable on its secured term loans today, with 787.6 US$m of cash and investments and 3.40 times leverage on Adjusted EBITDA, but depends on managing VIVITROL generic entry expected in 2027. | Medium | Covenant levels, cash interest and ownership are not in the sources, and leverage rests on management add-backs. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |
| Debt of 1,497.7 US$m is secured, with 89.1% of principal due in 2031 and only 164.2 US$m due before then. | Near-term amortization is light and refinancing risk sits in 2031. | High |
| Leverage is 3.40 times on Adjusted EBITDA but 10.25 times on reported EBITDA. | Credit strength depends on whether add-backs are accepted. | Medium |
| VIVITROL, 31.7% of FY2025 revenue, faces expected generic entry in 2027. | Cash flow from a legacy product may fall while debt remains. | Medium |
| LUMRYZ added 16.5% of nine-month 2026 revenue through four specialty pharmacies, with a generic challenge pending. | Growth is real but concentrated and legally exposed. | Medium |
| Free cash flow over the last twelve months was 227.4 US$m, equal to 15.2% of debt. | Debt can be reduced from cash flow if operating results hold. | Medium |
### Credit view

Alkermes plc is a moderately leveraged specialty drug company whose secured term loans look serviceable from current cash flow, but whose coverage depends on managing expected VIVITROL generic entry in 2027 and on integrating LUMRYZ. The strongest support is liquidity: USD 787.6 million of cash and investments against USD 26.5 million of principal due in 2027 and only USD 164.2 million due before 2031. The weakest point is that total debt of USD 1,497.7 million is 3.40x LTM Adjusted EBITDA but 10.25x reported EBITDA, so leverage rests on management add-backs, and covenant levels cannot be read. The outcome will be decided by whether legacy cash flow is replaced as VIVITROL erodes, and by the covenant terms not yet supplied.
### Key findings

Alkermes borrowed its full USD 1,525.0 million of term loans to buy Avadel, moving from no debt at December 31, 2025 to USD 1,497.7 million of senior secured debt at September 30, 2026. The debt is two bank term loans with no bonds. Scheduled principal is USD 6.625 million for the rest of 2026, USD 26.500 million in 2027, USD 40.563 million in 2028 and USD 45.250 million in each of 2029 and 2030, which leaves 89.1% of principal due in 2031 (new arithmetic, see Calculations) [financial base: debt and capital structure]. Liquidity of USD 787.6 million of cash and investments, with no revolver found, is what the creditor can rely on, and it comfortably covers amortization.

Leverage is the central judgement. On LTM Adjusted EBITDA of USD 440.2 million, total debt is 3.40x and net debt 1.61x, but LTM reported EBITDA is only USD 146.2 million, which gives 10.25x and 4.86x. The difference is acquisition costs, inventory step-up, share-based compensation and a contingent consideration charge, and the FY2025 part of LTM Adjusted EBITDA is derived by the analyst. Expense-basis cover is 5.08x on Adjusted EBITDA, with cash interest unreported [financial base: leverage and coverage].

Business risk is concentrated. VIVITROL was 31.7% of FY2025 revenue and generic entry is expected in 2027, while ARISTADA patents run to 2039 and LYBALVI patents to 2041, with LYBALVI facing paragraph IV challenges, and the legacy products rely on three wholesalers. LUMRYZ supplied 16.5% of nine-month 2026 revenue through four specialty pharmacies, bears a 3.85% royalty to Jazz and faces a generic challenge [business context: operating model and credit translations]. Cash from operations of USD 72.9 million for nine months 2026, against USD 350.7 million a year earlier, shows how heavily the first year of integration weighed on cash, while LTM free cash flow of USD 227.4 million shows the recovery to date [financial base: cash flow quality].

Documented behaviour is not extractive: no dividend has been paid and buybacks of USD 27.7 million occurred only in Q1 2026, but ownership, board and covenant capacity are not supplied, so legal capacity for distributions cannot be tested [business context: ownership, governance and capital allocation]. This corrects the business context handoff, which said buybacks stopped after the term loans were drawn: the sources show only that none occurred in Q2 or Q3 2026 and do not date the Q1 purchases against the February 12, 2026 closing.
### Strengths and weaknesses

Strengths. (1) Liquidity and maturity profile: USD 787.6 million of cash and investments against light amortization and a 2031-weighted maturity wall, which gives time to absorb the 2027 VIVITROL change (Documentary Fact; financial base). (2) Cash generation: LTM free cash flow of USD 227.4 million with low capital spending, equal to 15.2% of debt (Documentary Fact for the inputs; the ratio is Analyst Interpretation). (3) Portfolio breadth beyond one product: four proprietary products plus royalties, with ARISTADA patents to 2039, LYBALVI to 2041 and LUMRYZ orphan exclusivity to 2030 for adults (Documentary Fact; business context). (4) Interest rate protection on USD 750.0 million of notional through collars entered in October 2026, though covenant effects are unknown (Documentary Fact). (5) Documented financial behaviour has been conservative: debt prepaid in 2024, no dividends, no buybacks in Q2 or Q3 2026 (Documentary Fact; Analyst Interpretation on what it implies).

Weaknesses. (1) Dependence on add-backs: 3.40x on Adjusted EBITDA against 10.25x on reported EBITDA, with a derived FY2025 base and share-based compensation add-backs that do not tie to the statements (Documentary Fact; the dependence is Analyst Interpretation). (2) Product concentration and generic risk: VIVITROL at 31.7% of FY2025 revenue with generic entry expected in 2027, and product-level margins Not supplied, so the cash flow effect cannot be sized (Documentary Fact; Insufficient Information for the effect). (3) Secured structure without visible covenants: all debt is secured on substantially all assets, but levels, definitions and the margin grid are Not supplied, and Term Loan B is outside the maintenance tests (Insufficient Information). (4) Floating-rate exposure: Term SOFR plus 1.75% to 2.25% on Term Loan A and 2.25% on Term Loan B, half of principal hedged by collars (Documentary Fact; the share is arithmetic). (5) Acquisition accounting and contingent liability: a preliminary purchase price allocation, intangibles and goodwill that make up most of the consideration, and a possible payment of USD 165.7 million carried at USD 136.9 million (Documentary Fact; the impairment exposure is Analyst Interpretation). (6) Channel and counterparty concentration: three wholesalers for legacy products and four specialty pharmacies for LUMRYZ (Documentary Fact). (7) Thin interim cash conversion: nine-month 2026 cash from operations of USD 72.9 million (Documentary Fact).
### Credit assessment and thesis
| Element | Statement | Category | Confidence | Basis |

| Assessment | Fundamental credit view: moderately leveraged with adequate liquidity and a back-ended secured maturity profile; sensitive to VIVITROL erosion, add-back acceptance and unseen covenants | Analyst Interpretation | Medium | Financial base: debt, liquidity, leverage and cash flow; business context: operating model and credit translations |

| Thesis | Alkermes can service its USD 1,497.7 million of secured term loans from cash flow and liquidity, provided LUMRYZ and the other proprietary products offset the expected 2027 loss of VIVITROL exclusivity | Analyst Interpretation | Medium | Financial base: LTM free cash flow and maturity table; business context: revenue durability row |
| Liquidity | USD 787.6 million of cash and investments; undrawn committed facilities Not supplied | Documentary Fact | Medium | Financial base: liquidity |
| Covenant headroom | Not assessable from the sources | Insufficient Information | Not assessable | Missing credit agreement; matters because it decides default triggers |
### Key credit risks
| Risk | Mechanic | Credit implication | Severity | Basis |

| VIVITROL generic entry in 2027 | Substitution reduces volume and price of the largest FY2025 product at 31.7% of revenue | Lower cash flow against fixed debt service and a thinner path to 2031 refinancing | Material | Business context: revenue durability row; financial base: product shares |

| Add-back dependence | Management Adjusted EBITDA excludes costs that the statements bear; the FY2025 component is derived | Leverage and covenant measures may differ from the 3.40x shown | Material | Financial base: leverage and conflicts |

| Covenant opacity | Maintenance tests named but levels Not supplied; Term Loan B excluded | Default and amendment risk cannot be sized | Material | Financial base: covenants; source readiness: gaps |

| 2031 refinancing concentration | 89.1% of principal due in 2031, with Term Loan A and B 6 months apart | Refinancing depends on market access and operating performance in 2031 | Material | Financial base: debt maturities |

| Interest rate exposure | Floating-rate debt with Term SOFR at 4.07% at September 30, 2026; collars cover 750.0 US$m | Higher rates reduce coverage; cash interest is not reported | Minor | Financial base: debt and market risk |

| Acquisition and CVR | Preliminary allocation; a payment of up to USD 165.7 million may be due after the milestone | Additional cash claim and possible impairment | Minor | Business context: transaction summary |

| Patent litigation and rebate exposure | Paragraph IV suits for LYBALVI and LUMRYZ; gross-to-net adjustments of 47.7% of gross sales in Q3 2026 | Earlier generic entry or net price pressure | Material | Business context: credit translations |
| Counterparty concentration | Three wholesalers and four specialty pharmacies | Collection or channel disruption | Minor | Business context: customers and distribution row |
## Calculations
This module uses only handoff figures; the following are new arithmetic from them.

1. Share of principal due in 2031 and after: 1,347.562 / 1,511.750 = 89.1% (maturity table, financial base). Principal due 2026 to 2030: 6.625 + 26.500 + 40.563 + 45.250 + 45.250 = 164.188, shown as USD 164.2 million; 164.188 / 1,511.750 = 10.9%.
2. LTM free cash flow to debt: 227.368 / 1,497.731 = 15.2%.

3. Leverage sensitivity (illustrative, not a covenant test; debt held at USD 1,497.731 million): a 10% fall in LTM Adjusted EBITDA of 440.190 gives 396.171 and 1,497.731 / 396.171 = 3.78x; a 20% fall gives 352.152 and 4.25x. Reported EBITDA sensitivity is not computed.
4. Collar notional share: 750.0 / 1,511.750 = 49.6%, described in words as about half.
## Gaps

| FY2025 Adjusted EBITDA is derived; add-back differences with statements | LTM Adjusted EBITDA and the 3.40x inherit it | Leverage | Medium | Obtain the Q4 2025 release |
| Product-level margins and VIVITROL contribution Not supplied | The cash flow effect of 2027 generic entry cannot be sized | Revenue durability | Medium | Management or segment data if available |
| Ownership, board, and large holder data Not supplied | Control and alignment cannot be assessed beyond documented actions | Governance | Medium | Add proxy statement |
| Preliminary purchase price allocation; CVR milestone terms Not supplied | Goodwill, intangibles and contingent payment may change | Balance sheet | Medium | Monitor measurement period adjustments |
| Inherited readiness limits from the source readiness handoff (READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS) | Restricts confidence to Medium | All | Medium | See the three upstream gap lists |

Proceed to CP-5 (evidence trace validation) with all four handoffs; it should confirm that each CP-1 figure used here keeps its value, unit and period, that the 89.1%, 15.2% and sensitivity figures follow from them, and that the credit view does not assert covenant headroom, recovery outcomes or instrument preference.
